public_rationale: Reports establish substantial technology selling on November 16 following a broad selloff on Friday, November 13. This supports the ordinary reading that selling resumed after an episode late last week. However, the major benchmarks gained over the full preceding week. A claim that last week's aggregate market return was a rout would not be supported.
limitations: The outcome depends on reading last week's rout as an episode within the week.
Reputable market reporting substitutes for directly retrieved exchange data.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Tech stocks are dropping sharply as of 16 November 2026, after a rout the week before.

statement.excerpt: Tech stocks continue to drop sharply today, following on the rout we saw last week.

from_speaker: following on the rout we saw last week
our_interpretation: Today means November 16, 2026; last week means the trading sessions of November 9–13.
Tech stocks means a broad set of technology shares, checked against a technology-heavy index and named sector constituents.
The plain reading requires substantial selling today following a substantial selloff during the preceding week. It does not necessarily assert a negative return for that entire week.
Sharp and rout describe substantial, broad selling rather than a small routine fluctuation; no numerical threshold is supplied.
criteria.support_condition: Dated market reports show substantial technology-stock selling on November 16 and a broad technology selloff during November 9–13.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Technology shares were broadly stable or rising on November 16, or no substantial technology selloff occurred during the preceding trading week.

evidence.publisher: Associated Press, syndicated by The Week through PTI
evidence.explanation: The report records a 1.7% Nasdaq decline at 12:02 p.m. Eastern, alongside losses in Broadcom, AMD and CoreWeave. This supports substantial selling beyond Nvidia.
The report records Friday losses of 8.8% in AMD, 4.8% in Broadcom and 6.2% in Cisco. It establishes a substantial technology selloff during the preceding week.
This limits the claim: the late-week selloff did not make the major benchmarks' full-week returns negative. It contradicts a stronger reading that the entire week was a broad market rout.
